title: Capability policy
description: The normative description of `.agents/policies/<id>.yaml` (ADR 0015 §2). A policy is the enforcement source of truth for `packages/policy`, so unknown keys are rejected rather than ignored: a key that is silently dropped here produces a document that appears to constrain and does not.

id.description: Policy identifier. Optional, but must equal the file name when present.

description.description: Human-facing summary. Documentation only — the evaluator does not read it.

capabilities.description: Allow and deny lists per capability class. A class that is absent is unconstrained by this policy.

filesystem.description: Path globs the roles governed by this policy may read and write.

exec.description: Command prefixes the roles governed by this policy may run.

network.description: Network destinations the roles governed by this policy may reach.

limits.description: Resource ceilings. Note the snake_case keys, which differ from the camelCase fields the parsed policy exposes.

cost_usd.description: Spend ceiling in US dollars. Must be a positive finite number; the loader rejects anything else rather than dropping it.

confirmations.description: Action categories routed to human approval instead of a hard verdict.

required_for.description: snake_case alias of `requiredFor`. Both spellings are accepted, and `requiredFor` wins when a document declares both.

idToken.description: Letters, digits, '.', '_' and '-', starting with a letter or digit; never a path separator or '..', because these become path segments.

capabilityRules.description: Patterns for one capability class. Both lists are optional; deny takes precedence over allow at evaluation time.
